newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index sligthly up.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index sligthly up.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in thiner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with the SAX index edging up 0.11 points to 192.20 on gains to shares of oil and gas storage company Nafta.
Nafta gained 40 crowns to close at 1,860, on a rather high volume of 22,690 shares, but brokers considered the share overvalued and expected it to ease.

"The current Nafta price is too high to reflect its real value which I see at some 1,780 crows, and I expect the issue to resume downward trend ending at about this levels," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
Steel maker VSZ closed up one crown at 604, but its average price declined over the today session by 0.33 percent, which Sykora said was only a short-term correction.
"At present there is a relatively large volume of VSZ shares available on the market, and as it is one of the best issues, we expect an increase in its price soon," Sykora said.

Oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at 850 crowns, and dealers expected the issue to continue in downward trend, posted over the past few days, mainly as an effect of the overall bearish mood on the market.
VUB, the largest commercial bank, closed unchanged at 1,650, and its price was seen as hovering over its current levels in near future.
Overall volume increased to 604,927 shares, boosted by direct trades, from 386,740 shares traded on Monday, while the turnover fell to 166.99 million crowns, from 260.95 million.
